correctness.rationale: From \(A=\varphi(-z)\varphi(-z^2)=F^{-1}\), the correction \(C=(F^4-1)/8\) is integral, with \(C\) modulo \(2\) equal to the sum of the square and four-times-square exponent series. Thus \(AC^2\) has vanishing odd coefficients modulo \(2\). For \(t=2^{i-3}(2k+1)\), the quadratic binomial correction gains one extra factor of \(2\), and every term of order \(j\ge3\) has valuation at least \(i+6\). This gives the full odd-index lifting modulo \(2^{i+3}\). The signed-theta residue obstruction sets \(a(8n+5)=a(8n+7)=0\), and the published Saikia--Sarma Theorem 1.1 supplies the moduli \(32\) and \(64\) for the triple counts. The exact coefficients \(\bar b_3(5)=1248\), \(\bar b_3(7)=9792\), and \([z^7]AC^2=7424\) prove best-possible valuations. The packaged verifier checks two independent series constructions and \(1920\) finite lifting instances, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result proves both clauses of an explicitly stated 2026 conjecture for all unbounded parameters and proves the exact powers of \(2\) optimal for every allowed tuple index using the least two coefficient indices. The stronger odd-index congruence isolates an arithmetic parity cancellation that ordinary binomial-lifting bounds miss; it is a useful structural lemma, not a finite observation or a direct substitution into the triple theorem.
